prompt:
Reddit post, r/houseplants.
Title: My work plant is dying!

Hi, posting for the first time here. I have had money plants that I’ve grown in water before but this little guy has been difficult to grow. Can anyone tell me why it’s yellowing? And what’s that thing on its roots??? I keep him away from the window and I used to keep it in a mug. I’ve moved it to this coffee bottle hoping that maybe all it needs is more room. I’ve also started using drinking water in case the tap water is the issue.

It has been like this a week after I cut it from its parent plant. And it’s been almost a year now but it neither grows nor dies

I’m ngl I used to just top off the water thinking that they would get the oxygen from the air 🫣 my bad.

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
**Most likely: a year in never-changed water with nothing to feed on.** Roots breathe oxygen dissolved in the water. When the water is only topped off, bacteria feeding on dead bits use that oxygen up, so the roots have partly suffocated and rotted. The black crust on the roots and nodes is most likely dead tissue coated in bacterial or algal slime. Plain water, tap or drinking, also has almost no nutrients, so after a year the plant is starved: pale, yellowing leaves and no growth. Sitting away from the window slows it further.

**Also possible: scale insects.** The round brown bumps on the green stems could be scale, which also causes yellowing. If one flicks off with a fingernail like a tiny shell, remove them all, dab the spots with rubbing alcohol on a cotton bud, and check the leaf undersides and the parent plant. If they won't budge, ignore them.

**Fix:**
1. **Clean up.** Rinse the roots under lukewarm water, rubbing off the crud. Keep firm roots even if they're spotted. Snip off mushy or hollow ones, and cut any soft stem back to firm tissue, keeping at least one node.
2. **Replace all the water weekly instead of topping off.** Scrub the jar and refill with room-temperature water covering only the roots and lowest nodes.
3. **Feed it.** Starting in week two, add liquid houseplant fertilizer at a quarter of the label dose every other water change (every two weeks).
4. **More light.** Put it within a metre of the window but out of harsh direct sun, or under an LED desk lamp about 30 cm away during work hours.

That fresh white root in your photo is a good sign. More like it within a few weeks means it's recovering.
